query_text: Should all nationalities have the same voting rights?

message.content:
Based on international standards and human rights frameworks, the principle is that **all citizens of a country should have equal voting rights**, regardless of their specific nationality background (such as whether they acquired citizenship by birth or naturalization). However, voting rights are generally tied to citizenship rather than extending to all nationalities universally.

## Key International Standards

### Universal and Equal Suffrage for Citizens

International human rights law establishes that voting rights should be universal and equal **among citizens** of a country:

- **Article 25 of the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (ICCPR)** states: "Every citizen shall have the right and the opportunity, without any of the distinctions mentioned in article 2 and without unreasonable restrictions... to vote and to be elected at genuine periodic elections which shall be by universal and equal suffrage" (https://digitallibrary.un.org/record/637591/files/E_CN.4_Sub.2_213_Rev.1-EN.pdf)

- The **Universal Declaration of Human Rights (Article 21)** affirms that "everyone has the right to take part in the government of his country" through "periodic and genuine elections which shall be by universal and equal suffrage" (https://old.eef.md/media/files/files/studiu-legislatie-en_5499378.pdf)

- The **Inter-Parliamentary Union Declaration** states: "Every adult citizen has the right to vote in elections, on a non-discriminatory basis" and "every voter is entitled to exercise his or her right equally with others and to have his or her vote accorded equivalent weight to that of others" (https://www.idea.int/sites/default/files/publications/international-electoral-standards-guidelines-for-reviewing-the-legal-framework-of-elections.pdf)

### Non-Discrimination Among Citizens

Critically, international law **prohibits distinctions between citizens** based on how they acquired citizenship:

- The UN Human Rights Committee's **General Comment No. 25** clarifies that "no distinctions are permitted between citizens in the enjoyment of these rights on the grounds of race, colour, sex, language, religion, political or other opinion, national or social origin, property, birth or other status" and that "distinctions between those who are entitled to citizenship by birth and those who acquire it by naturalization may raise questions of compatibility with article 25" (https://cdn.osce.org/sites/default/files/f/documents/4/a/19154.pdf)

- The UN study on political rights states: "Every national of a country is entitled within that country to full and equal political rights without distinction of any kind" and "No one shall be denied nationality, or deprived of nationality, as a means of denying him or depriving him of political rights" (https://digitallibrary.un.org/record/642921/files/E_CN.4_830--E_CN.4_Sub.2_218-EN.pdf?ln=ar)

## The Citizenship Boundary

Voting rights are generally limited to **citizens/nationals** rather than all persons regardless of nationality:

- The Venice Commission's Code of Good Practice notes that "universal suffrage means in principle that all human beings have the right to vote and to stand for election. This right may, however, and indeed should, be subject to certain conditions" including nationality (https://www.europarl.europa.eu/cmsdata/270956/Session-1-Irene-Hadziabdic.pdf)

- The OHCHR confirms that "the right to vote may be subject only to reasonable restrictions, such as setting a minimum age limit" and that citizenship is generally a legitimate boundary (https://europe.ohchr.org/news-events/news/your-vote-your-right-foundations-right-vote-international)

## Variations: Non-Citizen Voting Rights

Some countries extend limited voting rights to non-citizens:

- **EU citizens** can vote in municipal and European Parliament elections in other EU member states where they reside
- Some countries (e.g., Sweden, Finland, Luxembourg) grant **third-country nationals** voting rights at the local level (https://migpolgroup.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/NEI-Policy-Brief-14Nov2024-FINAL.pdf)
- Belgium requires non-European citizens to formally commit to respecting the Constitution and laws as a condition for municipal voting rights

## Conclusion

The international standard is clear: **within each country, all citizens—regardless of whether they are citizens by birth or naturalization—should have equal voting rights**. Discrimination among citizens based on national origin or how citizenship was acquired is prohibited. However, voting rights are generally tied to citizenship, meaning not all nationalities (i.e., non-citizens) have voting rights in every country. Whether non-citizens should have voting rights remains a matter of national discretion, with some countries extending limited local voting rights to long-term residents.
